channel.title: New Relic Monitor
channel.description: Application updates for New Relic Monitor

item.title: Version 2.7.2
item.description:
What's New in v2.7.2

The Throughput chart under "Historical Performance Trends" read higher than the same application's throughput in New Relic — 323K rpm against New Relic's 258K for one service — while the summary card directly above the chart showed the New Relic figure. Two numbers, one label, a 25% gap.

New Relic's APM throughput chart is labelled "Web throughput": it counts web transactions. This app counted every transaction, including background and non-web work, so any service with significant background processing read high.

What changed

  • Throughput trends and the week-over-week comparison now count web transactions only, matching both New Relic's APM chart and the summary on each entity card
  • Applications with no web traffic — background workers, queue consumers — still report their full transaction rate rather than a misleading "0 rpm"
  • Browser applications are unaffected, and their trend panels load faster than in 2.7.1

Notes

  • Response time and error rate still count all transactions, so those two may still read differently from New Relic's web-only figures
  • No configuration changes required. All existing settings, API keys, and suppressions are preserved.

item.title: Version 2.7.1
item.description:
What's New in v2.7.1

Some monitored applications showed a healthy summary — throughput, response time, Apdex — while everything below it stayed empty. "Historical Performance Trends" read "Trends paused for this entity", and "Compared to Last Week" read "No Transaction events for this entity — nothing to compare". The same application charted normally in New Relic's own UI.

Both messages were wrong. Those applications do have data; the app was asking for it the wrong way.

What changed

  • Applications that report no Transaction events now fall back to metric timeslice data — the same source New Relic's own APM charts read — so trends and the week-over-week comparison populate instead of reporting "no data"
  • Response time, error rate, throughput, and Apdex all have timeslice equivalents; values now agree with the New Relic dashboard
  • Fixed an entity metadata query that failed to decode for every entity, which had silently dropped the application-ID and name filters from every query the app makes
  • Affected entities are no longer put into a trends quarantine, so "Trends paused" and its retry countdown stop appearing for them

Notes

  • The fallback runs only for APM applications whose Transaction data is genuinely missing, so applications that already worked issue no additional queries
  • No configuration changes required. All existing settings, API keys, and suppressions are preserved.

item.title: Version 2.6.0
item.description:
What's New in v2.6.0

Please note: some numbers change in this release, because they were wrong before. If you have been reading response times or Apdex scores out of this app, the values you see now will differ from last week's. The new ones match New Relic; the old ones did not.

Corrected numbers

  • Response time was understated 1000× — New Relic reports these durations in seconds and the app formatted them as milliseconds, so an application averaging 80 ms displayed as "0.080 ms"
  • Apdex was always scored against 0.5s, whatever the entity was configured with — a synthetic monitor set to 7s was scored as if every check had failed
  • A service that went from no errors to some errors was shown a green "+100% improvement" badge
  • Trend badges flapped on near-zero error rates; changes too small to matter now read as stable
  • The trend headline showed the latest sample rather than the window average, so a service averaging 2 rpm could read "0.0 rpm"
  • Units that never scaled — a 103-second average displayed as "103900.9 ms"
  • Background applications displayed "0.000 ms" instead of their real duration
  • Apdex read "1.0" on cards and "0.99" in the detail pane for the same entity

Browser, Synthetic, and Infrastructure entities now show metrics

  • Selecting one of these previously showed no performance metrics at all — the code existed but was gated to APM applications, so it could never run
  • Infrastructure hosts report CPU, memory, and network as their own metrics, rather than a CPU percentage labelled "Response Time" and formatted as milliseconds

Recent Activity

  • The clock icon in the header opens delivered and muted notifications, so you can review what quiet hours or a suppression kept from you

No configuration changes required. All existing settings, API keys, and suppressions are preserved.

item.title: Version 2.5.0
item.description:
What's New in v2.5.0

Compared to Last Week

  • APM entity details now show each metric against the same window an hour, a day, or a week earlier
  • A 1h / 24h / 1w picker chooses the comparison; 1w is the default because it accounts for day-of-week traffic
  • Knows each metric's polarity — rising response time is bad, rising Apdex is good
  • Changes under 10% read as "normal"; an empty earlier window reports "no baseline" instead of a false regression

Transactions (last hour)

  • Per-endpoint breakdown ranked by "Most Time" (duration × call count) or "Slowest" (highest average)
  • Switching rankings is instant — both come from a single query

Bug Fixes

  • The menu bar "Preferences..." item did nothing when clicked
  • ⌘, now opens Preferences
  • The Preferences "Cancel" button reverted nothing outside the API tab, and is now "Close"
  • First-run setup had no way out if you did not have an API key yet
  • Invalid API keys failed with a misleading "40+ characters" message

Documentation

  • Removed help content for shortcuts and features that were never implemented
  • Documented alert suppression, quiet hours, Copy as Markdown, launch at login, and the APM detail sections

No configuration changes required. All existing settings, API keys, and suppressions are preserved.

item.title: Version 2.3.0
item.description:
What's New in v2.3.0

Two New Relic-native additions to the entity detail view, plus the per-entity alert suppression fix from v2.2.0.

Errors (last hour)

  • APM detail views now list grouped application errors by class and message, with occurrence counts
  • Top 10 error groups ranked by count, with a header chip showing the total

Recent Deployments

  • APM detail views now show change-tracking deployment markers from the last 30 days
  • Each entry shows version, time, author, and a deep link into New Relic when available

Also included

  • Alert suppression now works per-alert instead of globally (from v2.2.0)

No configuration changes required. All existing settings and API keys are preserved.

item.title: Version 2.1.0
item.description:
What's New in v2.1.0

Major internal improvements for stability, performance, and reliability since v1.9.2.

Architecture (v2.0.0)

  • API Client Refactor - NewRelicAPIClient reduced from 2,365 to ~500 lines; delegates to focused service classes
  • UI Performance - Fewer SwiftUI re-renders during searches and filter changes
  • Memory Management - Entity cache now enforces 5-minute TTL and 500-entry max with LRU eviction
  • Thread Safety - GraphQL rate limiting protected by NSLock; EntityService marked @MainActor
  • Error Visibility - All silent failures now log context for debugging

Service Hardening (v2.1.0)

  • Credential Handling - Safer nil/empty API key handling across all services
  • Notification Reliability - More robust permission checking and delivery
  • Dynamic Versioning - About window always shows the correct version
  • Expanded Tests - 690+ lines of new unit test coverage

No configuration changes required. All existing settings and API keys are preserved.
